ace_dust_content_cosmic_noon.summary: A new ALMA study of 25 star‑forming galaxies at z≈2.3 reveals dust masses around 10⁸ M⊙, three‑to‑nine times larger than comparable local galaxies.
highlights: Dust masses average 10⁸ M⊙, far exceeding local counterparts at similar metallicity
Dust‑to‑stellar mass ratio stays near 10⁻²·² regardless of metallicity
Specific star‑formation rates above 10⁻⁸ yr⁻¹ drive the elevated dust‑to‑stellar ratios

2609_21333v1.headline: Patchy Reionization Delays Star‑Formation Quenching in Isolated Ultra‑Faint Dwarfs
2609_21333v1.summary: High‑resolution zoom‑in simulations show that a radiative‑transfer patchy reionization model postpones quenching in ultra‑faint dwarf galaxies by roughly 440 Myr compared with uniform UV background.
highlights: Patchy reionization model delays quenching by ~440 Myr on average.
Uniform UVB simulations truncate star formation abruptly at reionization onset.
Extended star formation leaves no clear signature in stellar metallicity distribution.
Results align with recent observational constraints on Local Group ultra‑faint dwarf star‑formation histories.

nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.institution: University of Science and Technology of China
nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.headline: Nuclear‑spin swap boosts room‑temperature entanglement lifetime by 240‑fold
nuclear_spin_swap_entanglement.summary: Researchers at the University of Science and Technology of China swapped electron entanglement into silicon‑29 nuclei, extending coherence to over 240 µs at room temperature.
highlights: Entanglement persisted for more than 240 µs after transfer to nuclear spins, versus ~1 µs in the electron alone
The SWAP‑gate protocol retained 92.5% fidelity, only slightly below the initial 94%
Over 10% of 200 surveyed silicon‑carbide color centers hosted two or more strongly coupled silicon‑29 nuclei

exoplanet_radio_detection.headline: MeerKAT Detects Radio Waves from Beta Pictoris b, Hinting at Extraterrestrial Auroras
exoplanet_radio_detection.summary: For the first time scientists have traced circularly‑polarized radio emissions directly to the gas giant Beta Pictoris b, suggesting a powerful aurora and magnetic field.
highlights: Radio waves were observed with the MeerKAT telescope in South Africa
The emissions are linked to Beta Pictoris b, a 10‑Jupiter‑mass planet 63 light‑years away
Polarization indicates a magnetic field exceeding 1,000 gauss, far stronger than Earth’s
The detection overcomes previous challenges of separating planetary signals from stellar noise

alzheimer_mri.headline: MRI Reveals Subtle Cortical Thickening Up to Seven Years Before Alzheimer’s Diagnosis
alzheimer_mri.summary: Researchers found that individuals who later develop high amyloid‑beta levels show a few hundredths of a millimeter thicker cortex up to seven years prior to PET‑confirmed disease.
highlights: Cortical thickness differences of only a few hundredths of a millimeter were detectable up to seven years before amyloid‑beta
Study analyzed MRI data from over a thousand participants in long‑term aging cohorts
Both groups showed natural age‑related thinning, but future Alzheimer’s cases thinned less overall
Findings suggest early-stage inflammation may cause transient cortical thickening

equivalence_principle_tests.headline: Space‑borne atom interferometer delivers most precise quantum test of Einstein’s equivalence principle
equivalence_principle_tests.summary: A cold‑atom interferometer on the China Space Station achieved a 2.8 × 10⁻⁸ uncertainty, confirming the weak equivalence principle for 85Rb and 87Rb isotopes.
highlights: Cold atom interferometry on the China Space Station measured a differential acceleration of –2.7 × 10⁻⁷ between 85Rb and 87Rb
The experiment collected over 9,700 interference‑fringe pairs during a 280‑day mission
A separate Quantum Galileo Interferometer in Israel verified the same gauge phase for a free‑falling 87Rb wavepacket
Both studies were published in Science Advances and report peer‑reviewed results
The teams plan next‑generation tests using nanodiamond particles to probe higher‑mass quantum objects

brain_two_organs_discovery.headline: Stanford Study Shows Human Brain Developed from Two Separate Evolutionary Organs
brain_two_organs_discovery.summary: Researchers discovered that distinct progenitor cells form the forebrain and hindbrain, revealing an ancient split that reshapes our understanding of brain development.
highlights: Forebrain and midbrain arise from Otx2‑expressing progenitors, while hindbrain derives from Gbx2‑expressing cells
Team grew functional human hindbrain motor neurons in vitro for the first time
Evolutionary analysis shows the two‑origin pattern exists in chickens, zebrafish and acorn worms

early_mars_water_systems.headline: Perseverance Finds Complex Multi‑Stage Water Interactions in Mars’ Jezero Crater Margin Unit
early_mars_water_systems.summary: NASA’s Perseverance rover uncovered igneous rocks in Jezero’s Margin Unit that record at least three distinct water events, reshaping ideas of early Martian habitability.
highlights: SuperCam laser analyses of 185 bedrock targets revealed sequential water‑rock reactions
Olivine-rich rocks show carbonate and silica formation from groundwater and lake water
Fluorite‑bearing veins indicate a later hot, underground water episode
Findings published in Communications Earth & Environment challenge prior carbonate‑only models

direct_imaging_subparsec_binary_smbhs_ng.headline: VLBA Images Reveal Sub-Parsec Binary Supermassive Black Holes in NGC 5044
direct_imaging_subparsec_binary_smbhs_ng.summary: VLBA observations have directly imaged two compact, flat‑spectrum radio cores separated by 0.38 pc, constituting the tightest binary AGN ever seen.
highlights: Two radio cores show flat spectra and variability
Separation measured at 0.38 parsec, an order of magnitude tighter than previous binaries
Observations span 4.9, 8.4, 15.2 and 23.6 GHz frequencies

2609_22466v1.headline: Model‑Independent Probe Reveals Baryon Depletion Around Galaxies via Lensing and kSZ
2609_22466v1.summary: A new technique combining DESI galaxy‑galaxy lensing with ACT kinematic Sunyaev‑Zel'dovich maps measures radial gas fractions, finding significant baryon loss relative to the cosmic mean.
highlights: Detected baryon depletion with signal‑to‑noise ratios of 17.1 (BGS) and 15.8 (LRG)
Method applies identical ΔΣ aperture filters to shear and kSZ temperature maps
Results lie between the strongest (Illustris‑1) and weaker feedback models from six simulations
Robust against splits by stellar mass and central versus satellite galaxies

gc_gamma_ray_and_neutrino_multi_messenge.headline: HAWC and IceCube Probe Galactic Center Gamma Rays for Neutrino Signals
gc_gamma_ray_and_neutrino_multi_messenge.summary: Using 2860 days of HAWC data and 12 years of IceCube muon-track observations, researchers find no neutrino excess from the Galactic Center, setting first upper limits.
highlights: HAWC detects gamma‑ray emission up to >100 TeV from the Galactic Center region
Analysis reveals a point source HAWC J1745‑2857 plus diffuse Galactic emission
IceCube’s 12‑year muon‑track data show no corresponding neutrino signal, placing an upper limit ~12× the predicted flux
The limit does not yet rule out the optically thin hadronic scenario for PeV cosmic‑ray acceleration

extreme_precision_radial_velocity_survey.headline: Galactic‑scale extreme‑precision radial velocity survey targets subgiant stars to map Milky Way acceleration
extreme_precision_radial_velocity_survey.summary: A new ESPRESSO survey of quiet subgiant stars within one kiloparsec aims to measure Galactic accelerations with ~50 cm s⁻¹ precision over a decade.
highlights: ESPRESSO on the VLT achieved ~70 cm s⁻¹ precision, now improved to ~50 cm s⁻¹
The "gold" sample comprises subgiant stars selected for minimal stellar jitter
Survey seeks direct constraints on the Milky Way’s dark‑matter distribution

grb_220706a_month_long_engine.headline: GRB 220706A Shows Record‑Breaking Month‑Long Engine and Bright Supernova
grb_220706a_month_long_engine.summary: Observations of GRB 220706A reveal central engine activity lasting 27 days in its rest frame and a super‑luminous supernova peaking at M_r ≤ ‑20.25.
highlights: X‑ray flares persisted until ≈51 days after trigger, the longest engine activity recorded
Redshift z = 0.8577 places the event at a cosmological distance
The associated supernova rivals SN 2011kl in brightness, fitting the super‑luminous class

thermal_relic_constraints_from_desi_lyma.headline: DESI Lyman‑α Forest Tightens Limits on Sterile Neutrinos and Extra Radiation
thermal_relic_constraints_from_desi_lyma.summary: Using DESI DR1 Lyman‑α power spectrum with Planck 2018 CMB and DESI DR2 BAO data, researchers find no evidence for extra relativistic species or sterile neutrinos.
highlights: Combined DESI DR1 1D Lyα power spectrum with Planck 2018 CMB and DESI DR2 BAO measurements.
Upper bound N_eff < 3.41 (95% credibility) shows no extra radiation.
Sterile neutrino effective mass constrained to m_s^eff < 0.061 eV.
ΔN_eff limits imply decoupling temperatures as high as the QCD epoch.

2609_23428v1.headline: Dark Matter Subhalos Could Skew Gravitational‑Wave Lens Time Delays
2609_23428v1.summary: Millisecond‑precise gravitational‑wave observations reveal that subhalos of 10⁶–10⁹ M☉ can perturb lensing time delays by several hours, challenging current analyses.
highlights: NFW‑profile subhalos introduce hour‑scale time‑delay anomalies in fold and cusp lens configurations
Current GW detectors achieve millisecond timing, far finer than the few‑hour precision of electromagnetic lensing
Statistical analysis of 200 realizations shows no milli‑images, but predicts measurable delay perturbations

2609_22424v1.headline: Quasar Outflows Linked from Broad‑Line Region to Galactic Scales
2609_22424v1.summary: A study of 148 ultra‑luminous quasars (Lbol > 10^47 erg s⁻¹, z ≈ 2–6.5) finds correlated CIV emission and BAL velocities, indicating BLR clouds accelerate to galaxy‑scale outflows.
highlights: Statistically significant correlations between CIV emission v98 and BAL vmin,BAL/vmax,BAL were detected.
High‑redshift quasars show larger CIV line shifts, broader profiles, and faster BAL outflows than lower‑redshift counterparts.
The sample spans redshifts z ≈ 2–6.5, probing cosmic‑time evolution of AGN‑driven winds.

inflated_sms_lrds.headline: JWST’s Little Red Dots May Be Inflated Supermassive Stars Pre‑cursor to Black Holes
inflated_sms_lrds.summary: New 1D models suggest metal‑rich supermassive stars with inflated envelopes could explain JWST’s abundant high‑redshift little red dots and seed supermassive black holes.
highlights: Models with metallicity Z≈10⁻² produce envelopes at Teff≈7000 K
Maximum non‑rotating masses reach 3×10⁵ Msun, luminosities ~10⁴⁴ erg s⁻¹
If each LRD collapses, predicted remnant density is ~10⁻² cMpc⁻³

stereoscopic_gravitational_wave_probe.headline: Gravitational‑Wave Lensing by AGN Disks Offers Dual‑View of Binary Mergers
stereoscopic_gravitational_wave_probe.summary: If many compact binary coalescences occur in active galactic nucleus accretion disks, their gravitational waves can be lensed to produce two distinct viewing angles detectable by current and future detectors.
highlights: LIGO‑Virgo‑KAGRA may observe multiple GW "images" from a single binary orbiting a supermassive black hole
The two images differ in effective viewing angle and exhibit a relativistic Doppler shift
A single extra parameter suffices to model AGN‑lens systems when the AGN spin aligns with the binary’s orbital angular momentum

wavedriver_lgs_ao.headline: WaveDriver Concept Shows Feasibility for Laser‑Guide‑Star AO on Habitable Worlds Observatory
wavedriver_lgs_ao.summary: Initial modeling and testbed experiments indicate the WaveDriver laser guide star system can achieve the picometer‑level wavefront stability required for the Habitable Worlds Observatory.
highlights: High Contrast Testbed demonstrated stability metrics approaching the required picometer precision
Multiple deformable mirrors and coronagraphs were integrated to assess sensor performance
Optical model quantifies LGS brightness, conjugation errors, and field errors from finite beacon separation

2609_23091v1.headline: Super‑Earth Interiors Contract by ~10% as Silicate Mantles Crystallise
2609_23091v1.summary: New PROTEUS simulations show that volatile‑poor super‑Earths shrink by about ten percent during mantle solidification, largely independent of mass.
highlights: Silicate interiors of 1‑10 Earth‑mass super‑Earths contract ~10 % as they cool
Volatile‑rich planets ≥5 Earth masses may retain deep magma oceans, limiting contraction
Contraction depends on mantle thinning, not host star irradiation or initial thermal state
